Cross-section footnotes:
- [^13] "William James" (author name span, frontmatter source line): pass. It is the first naming of the author in the note, so the later "my"/"I" statements resolve. No cut of the "I" in "Pragmatism says no, and I fully agree with her" would carry the agreement without leaving the "I" dangling.
- [^23] "the Absolute of transcendental idealism" (section "Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion"): pass. It names the same Absolute that James called "majestic" and "sterile" there and returns to here.
- [^26] "to let the world wag in its own way" (section "Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion"): pass. In that section it is the appositive gloss on "moral holiday", so it names the right referent. The splice reads slightly awkwardly but is still a sentence.
